title: fix(fields): drop a `between` row until both bounds are filled in
body:
Fixes #9914

`condToMongo`'s `between` arm handed both value boxes straight to `coerceByType`, which returns `''` unchanged (its `value !== ''` conjunct). A range the admin had half typed therefore travelled `handleBuilderChange` -> `filterGroupToMongo` -> `onChange(JSON.stringify(mongo))` into a stored `sys_sharing_rule.criteria_json`. The existing operator pin exercises `between` with a COMPLETE pair only, so the half-filled case had never been driven.

## Reproduced first, not inferred

Driven through a real render of the widget under its actual contract (a parent that stores what it emits and hands it back). What `onChange` received, verbatim:

| step | what `onChange` got |
|:--|:--|
| seed row added | `{"signed_on":""}` |
| operator switched to **Between** | `{"signed_on":{}}` |
| stored number range `{"age":{"$gte":1,"$lte":5}}`, upper box cleared | `{"age":{"$gte":1,"$lte":""}}` |

Two readings the card did not carry, both from that run:

1. **The dropdown offers `between` only on date-like columns** (`operatorsForFieldType`'s buckets — the number bucket has no `between`). The card's headline `{"age": ...}` document is real, but it is reached through the **stored-criteria** path: `kvToCondition` reads any two-key `$gte`/`$lte` back as a `between` row whatever the column type, so a saved number range renders two editable bounds and clearing one authors the blank bound. Measured above.
2. **Picking `Between` on a fresh row already broke the widget before any bound was typed.** The builder clears both bounds to `[]`, `JSON.stringify` drops the two `undefined`s, and `{"signed_on":{}}` reaches storage. `kvToCondition` cannot read that back, so `mongoToFilterGroup` returned null, the widget forced ITSELF into the raw-JSON editor and the toggle back was disabled. `between` was unreachable through the visual builder at all — objectui#8748's shape, on a second operator. Same arm, same repair.

## What the matcher does with each document

Measured against `ValueDataSource`'s real matcher over four rows (ages 0, 1, 5, 9) — because "omit the bound" and "emit the empty string" are different documents:

| criteria | rows matched |
|:--|:--|
| `{"age":{"$gte":1,"$lte":""}}` | **0 of 4** — the upper-bound comparison reads `''` as `0`, so no age passes it; the rule silently shares nothing |
| `{"age":{"$gte":"","$lte":5}}` | 3 of 4 — includes a row the real lower bound would have excluded, because `''` compares as `0` |
| `{"age":{}}` | **4 of 4** — every record. On a sharing rule that is an over-share, and `isMatchAllCriteria` does not catch it: a field key holding a nested object is not one of the vacuous shapes it recognises |
| `{"age":{"$gte":1}}` | 3 of 4 — a real one-sided predicate |
| `{"age":{"$gte":1,"$lte":5}}` | 2 of 4 — the range actually being typed |

## The question this card asked first: what was the divergence for?

`FilterConditionField` keeps its own completeness rule instead of delegating to `isFilterValueComplete`, and its comment states two reasons: `equals ''` is **a REAL predicate here that has to keep being emitted** ("the field is the empty string" is a filter an admin can mean) while that helper calls it unfinished; and adopting it would make this drop **depend on a helper marked internal in another package, whose vocabulary is the dropdown's rather than the spec's**.

Neither reason is about `between`. The divergence's actual subject is **the emitted document** versus the dropdown's notion of a finished row — and by that test an `''` bound is not a predicate an admin can mean (the table above), while `equals ''` is. So this change does **not** delegate: it adds a local, document-reasoned drop for one operator, leaves `equals ''` and every other arm untouched, and imports nothing new. The divergence comment is amended in place so it stays true rather than being quietly outgrown.

## The shape, and why it is the tree's shape rather than a fourth one

Drop the row; do not narrow it to the bound that is filled. That is already ruled here three times over — `isFilterValueComplete` ("a range missing an end is not a narrower range, it is a query the server refuses"), the view fold ("what is not applied is not persisted") and `sanitizeViewOverride`, which strips a half-filled pair on the read path. `filter-builder.tsx`'s own pair renderer already says the write path drops the cleared shape; this widget was the write path that did not. Refusing with a new per-row message would have invented a fourth behaviour and needed vocabulary outside this surface; dropping the only row already surfaces the existing red "criteria required" hint.

## Pins — the document that comes out, both directions

`packages/fields/src/widgets/__tests__/FilterConditionField.betweenBlankBound-9914.test.tsx`, 14 assertions over both reachable paths:

- the dropdown path on a date column: nothing emitted on pick, nothing on one bound, exactly the range on two, withdrawn again when a bound is cleared — plus a sweep asserting no document emitted during the whole interaction carries a blank bound or a vacuous field object;
- the stored-criteria path: clearing a bound of a saved number range withdraws the criteria instead of storing the blank bound;
- the other direction, which is what stops the drop over-reaching: a complete range emits exactly what it did before, `0` and `false` stay real bounds, `equals ''` and `greaterOrEqual ''` still emit, and the emitted range still round-trips through `kvToCondition`;
- the migration claim: a criteria already stored with a blank bound still loads into the builder and is not rewritten on mount.

## Ablation

Committed the fix first, then deleted the guard line, proved the mutation landed by blob hash (`cfc755264…` -> `f205024bb…`, anchor count 1 -> 0), ran the pin, restored with a trap on EXIT/INT/TERM using absolute paths, and proved restoration by hash equality plus an empty `git diff HEAD`.

Ablated: **9 failed, 4 passed of 14.** The four that stayed green are precisely the over-reach guards — old and new code agree on a complete range, on `0`/`false`, on the other operators and on the round-trip — so the ablation value is one the two implementations genuinely disagree about.

## Verification

All run through the shared verify lock; each `VERDICT` line read, never a bare exit status.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/fields/` — `Test Files 170 passed (170)`, `Tests 2927 passed (2927)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`, at `b7e48935e`.
- the conceptual neighbours (pair completeness, operator locale parity, the view fold's pair and empty-value pins, the overlay pair pin, the ValueDataSource filter-logic conformance pin, the README operator table) — `Test Files 8 passed (8)`, `Tests 177 passed (177)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields type-check` (both tsconfigs, so the tests are covered) — `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The dependency closure was built first; a fresh worktree's `TS2307` is a prerequisite, not a gate.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields lint` — exit 0, 0 errors (pre-existing warnings only).
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major` — all exit 0 at the final commit.

## Sweep and adjacency

Tests naming the changed file: four co-located `FilterConditionField.*` files plus the two `packages/fields` widget-registry sweeps — all inside the tree run above. Five test files elsewhere name it in **prose only**; two of those read files from disk, and neither path is this one. Nothing outside `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` imports the widget module.

Adjacency re-derived from **file lists of all 12 open pull requests**, never a title and never a branch name: no open pull request touches `FilterConditionField.tsx`; the only `packages/fields` overlap anywhere is a dependency bump touching that package's `package.json`.

## Pending-changeset sweep

Six pending changesets name this widget. None is made false: the objectui#8748 body is about the five text operators and its statements (value-less operators untouched, `equals ''` untouched) still hold; objectui#9001 and objectui#8976 refer to the `$icontains` producer half; the pair-completeness body concerns `sanitizeViewOverride` in another package, which this change makes the tree more consistent with, not less. `check:changeset-claims` agrees mechanically: no pending changeset names a file this change touches.
